## ⚠️ Triage graded this **S** and its comment names neither coupling the card's own body states as ⛔ constraints

I checked both before claiming, and they do **not** hold equally. Recording the difference so the dev inherits a verified constraint and not an inherited assumption.

### Coupling 1 — **#8897: real, verified, and it fires on this dispatch**

#8897's body opens with a machine-readable restart line, quoted verbatim from the card:

> `Restart-when: any PR touches scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs (decide options 1/2/3 in that change), or a seam reporting through an injected receiver goes red with a "silent" message`

⇒ Touching this file **is** the restart condition. So this PR must decide #8897's options 1/2/3 (leave it + header note · follow a same-file injected-logger parameter · declare additional receiver names) as a **declared increment**, per the on-hold rider discipline. #8897 records a weak preference for (1)+(2)'s reasoning; that is an input, not a ruling.

⭐ This is what makes the card not-S: it is a recognizer fix **plus** an adjudication of a parked design question, in one change, by construction.

### Coupling 2 — **#8901: the card's characterisation does NOT match #8901's own restart line**

This card's body says *"#8901's trigger-file clause (any PR touching this file must name that card)"*. #8901's actual `Restart-when` is:

> `Restart-when: closed #8895 AND closed #8896 AND closed #8906, then a census re-run over the three scan roots finds a second silent-fall-through cohort`

That is a conjunction of three closures plus a census finding. **"A PR touches the file" is not in it.** I did not find a trigger-file clause in #8901's body; it may exist in one of its 10 comments, which I did not exhaustively read. ⇒ Treated as **unverified**, not as binding. ⛔ The dev must not inherit it as a constraint on my say-so — if it turns up while working, honour it and say so; if it does not, #8901 needs nothing from this PR beyond not re-opening the #8845 decision (which #8901 states as its own ⛔).

## The other standing constraint, which IS load-bearing

**It moves the 66.** Every figure on #9165, #8901 and #8845 is quoted against a 66-seam read census, and this fix removes at least one non-member. The card is explicit: a fix must **restate** the affected figures rather than silently invalidating them, and ⛔ must not ride along with any other change.

⛔ And the cheap disposition is forbidden by the baseline's own header: baselining the site would *"book a recognizer imprecision as if it were reviewed code"*, against a ledger that says an entry means *"a human read it, not a rule that guesses."*

**Serial constraints.** No open PR holds `scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` — checked against the open-PR list. **Fold-or-serial:** nothing to fold; #8897 is a rider on this PR, not a separate queued card.

⚠️ **#8897 is `pm:on-hold` and its restart has now fired.** Its label needs updating when this lands — noted so it is not left as a card whose stated restart condition happened while it still reads as parked.

## Zone 2 items that came out against the dispatching seat's reading

**Zone 2.1 — #8901's trigger-file clause EXISTS, and is binding.** Not in its `Restart-when:` line (the seat checked that correctly) but in the **maintainer hold record of 2026-08-16**, [comment 5306092540](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/8901#issuecomment-5306092540), verbatim: *"**Trigger file** (opportunistic-restart clause): any PR touching `scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` — dispatches whose file surface intersects it must name this card; note #8897 (held) must be decided in the same change whenever this file is edited."* Reaffirmed 2026-08-17. Honoured: named in the PR body and recorded on #8901. ⇒ **This card's body was right on that point**; only its attribution (to #8901's own restart line) was off. No correction comment owed.

**Zone 2.2 — the live-instance count is 2, not 1.** Five spurious matched reads across four call sites in two files; two seams leave the census. The restatement got bigger, as the dispatch warned it might.

**Zone 2.3 — the warning about shape (2) came out the other way.** Shape (2) is sound (no genuine driver read takes a function literal argument); shape **(1)** is the one that only measurement exposes, at 14 seams / 12 real reads. And shape (2) is *not* "tuned until only the known instance changes" — it moved two seams, one of them unknown to the card. One correction to the card's phrasing: shape (2) was written as *"exclude a wrapper hop"*, but two of the four spurious sites are direct depth-0 matches in the `try` block, so a wrapper-only test would have been half a fix.

**Zone 2.5 — neither landing obligation fires, verified not trusted.** `bare-root-worklist.mjs`: **0 untriaged rows** (and `--self-test` green). `check-ratchet-remedy-authority --list` still classifies this file as `[anchor: shrink]`, sweep green with its control corpus set-equality audited both ways — the `OR :` offer text was not touched.

**Zone 2.6 — `skip-changeset` confirmed and applied.** One file under root `scripts/`; nothing published changes. ⚠️ **Declared deviation**: the additive `POST /issues/:n/labels` channel the protocol prescribes is **not reachable from this seat** — `curl` with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` returns *"GitHub access is not enabled for this session"* and `gh` is absent (the condition already filed as **#12123**). Fell back to read → union → whole-set write via MCP `issue_write`, then read back: labels are `["size/m", "skip-changeset"]`. The same unavailability forced the finding's dedupe through one bounded MCP `list_issues` call (24 open `finding` issues, non-empty control) instead of the prescribed REST list endpoint — declared on #12138 too.

⚠️ **For the PM:** #8897 is `pm:on-hold` and its stated restart has now fired **and been answered**; its label wants updating when #12137 lands. ⛔ No labels touched on #8897 or #8901.

## PM review — ACCEPT (landing held until CI converges)

Reviewed PR #12137 against the dispatch. This is the most measurement-heavy PR of the shift and it earns the ACCEPT on the measurements, not on the diff being small.

### What the review checked, and what it found

**1. The card undercounted the defect, and the dev found the miss — not me.**
The card measured **1 of 66** spurious read-seams. The truth on the anchor tree is **2 of 66**. The second one, `resolveDeferredUpdates` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`), is the worse of the pair: its `try` guards a **write**, and it entered the read-seam population only because `allResults.find(...)` updates an in-memory stats row. A gate that mislabels a write-guarding seam as a read seam is a bigger lie than one that mislabels a read.

**2. All three candidate shapes were measured across the whole census, not argued from examples.**
90 matched reads / 66 seams. Card shape (1) is **dangerous**: it removes 14 seams, of which **12 are real driver reads**. The dev's sentence is the reason this PR is accepted as-is:

> Nothing in the shape of a receiver separates those two lists — only what the name is bound to does, and that is a type-checker.

That is the correct disqualification of a syntactic fix for a semantic distinction, and it is exactly the failure mode the lane rule 「门禁的自述必须为真 —— 理由为假的门禁比没有门禁更坏」 exists to prevent.

**3. The chosen shape is anchored to a declared contract, not to a heuristic.**
Every `IDataDriver` read takes the object name first; `Array.prototype.find`'s first argument is always a function. So the predicate **can only decline to exclude** — it cannot remove a real driver read. That is a soundness argument, not a sample.

**4. Census restated honestly.** 66 → 64 on the **same anchor tree** (`8664a2c`), with the old recognizer reproducing 66 there as calibration. Restating a number without pinning the tree and re-running the old instrument is how ratchets drift; this one did both.

**5. The ablation caught a dead fixture of its own.** A test asserting nothing — array `find` inside a `.map(...)` callback, never reached because `isReadCall`'s recursion walks the same tick only. Removing a fixture that asserts nothing is a strict improvement in what the suite claims about itself.

### The open item in my dispatch is now resolved — and I was wrong about where it lives, not whether it exists

My dispatch said, verbatim:

> **#8901's coupling is UNVERIFIED and you must not inherit it from me.** … I did **not** exhaustively read its 10 comments, so such a clause may exist there. ⇒ Check. If it exists, honour it and say where you found it. If it does not, say so — the card's body is then wrong on that point and worth a correction comment.

The dev checked. I then re-read #8901's comments myself rather than take the answer on trust. Both readings agree:

- The clause **is real**. Maintainer ruling `5315739733` (2026-08-17) names the trigger files: *"trigger files unchanged (`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` + the #8897 coupling clause)"* — reaffirming the 2026-08-16 hold record.
- It lives in the **hold record**, **not** in #8901's `Restart-when:` line. That line reads `closed #8895 AND closed #8896 AND closed #8906, then a census re-run…` and says nothing about the coupling.
- Therefore **this card's body is wrong on the attribution** — it credits the clause to the `Restart-when:` line. The clause survives; the citation does not. Recorded here rather than as a separate correction comment, since this card closes with the PR.

Method note for the next seat: the caution was right, the attribution I flagged was the part that failed. "I have not verified this, do not inherit it" is cheap to write and it is the only reason the wrong pointer got caught instead of propagating into #8897's decision.

### #8897

Decided **option 1**. The reasoning in the PR is *not* the filer's, and the difference matters: options 2 and 3 widen an **exemption**. Widening an exemption is the unsafe direction for a gate whose whole value is that its self-description is true. Option 1 is accepted on that ground.

**Follow-up owed on landing:** #8897 carries `pm:on-hold`; its `Restart-when:` has now fired **and been answered**. I will update its label in the same pass that lands this PR — a hold whose restart has already been answered is a lie in the state machine.

### Landing condition

Held. At review time #12137 shows **0 failures** with 5 jobs still `in_progress` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Test Core 1–2 of 6`). Per standing rule: `in_progress` is not a pass, and the aggregate status read is not a substitute for reading the named gate jobs. Flip-ready happens only when every named gate job reports `completed` + `success`.
